title: We have twelve years of GNSS base-station data from our network of five permanent reference stations across northern Vojvodina, but we are not using it for anything beyond standard RTK corrections; we suspect there is value in the data for subsidence monitoring or infrastructure deformation tracking, but we don't know how to start.

record.text: We have twelve years of GNSS base-station data from our network of five permanent reference stations across northern Vojvodina, but we are not using it for anything beyond standard RTK corrections; we suspect there is value in the data for subsidence monitoring or infrastructure deformation tracking, but we don't know how to start.
record.detail: Since 2012 we have logged continuous RINEX observation data from five permanent reference stations placed across northern Vojvodina, mainly Subotica, Kanjiža, Senta, Ada, and Bečej. The stations were built to provide RTK corrections for our field crews and for a handful of licensed subscribers, and that is still their primary job. But twelve years of daily position solutions sitting on a RAID array feels like a resource we are not using. We have heard that networks like this can detect millimetre-level ground movement over time, which would be directly relevant to monitoring road embankments, canal levees, and the older building stock in our area, some of which sits on unstable loess. We downloaded one academic paper on GNSS time-series analysis and quickly ran into processing steps we did not understand. We have the raw RINEX data, station metadata, and antenna calibration logs. We do not have geodetic software licences beyond what we use for RTK processing, and we do not have staff with a background in time-series statistics. A practical outcome would be a pilot report showing whether any of our five stations show a detectable trend, with a workflow we could apply ourselves going forward.
